questions.q: Which description fits Apache Iceberg best?
options: A database that stores your rows
A layer that tracks which files make up a table
A tool that runs your queries
questions.explain: Iceberg is a table format. It keeps track of the files, columns and history of a table, while engines run the queries, and a file format such as Parquet holds the data inside each file.

questions.q: A load went wrong and bad rows landed in your table. Which Iceberg feature helps you get back to a good state?
questions.explain: Iceberg keeps snapshots of the table, so you can reset the table to an earlier good one. Hidden partitioning is about fast queries, not undoing mistakes.

questions.q: Your team has one small database and an app that updates single rows all day. Do you need Iceberg?
options: Probably not, the database already fits the job
Yes, because it replaces the database
Only if you rename your columns
questions.explain: Iceberg is built for large analytic tables shared by several tools. An app that needs fast single-row updates is a database job.

questions.q: A vendor says its tool 'supports Iceberg'. What is the smartest next step?
options: Assume it does everything Iceberg can do
Read its docs for limits, such as read-only tables or supported catalogs
questions.explain: Each engine supports different parts of Iceberg. Some tables are read-only in one tool, and some tools work with only one catalog, so check the limits first.
